clue.text: Discuss and study poetry

parts.note: to con is an old verb meaning to study or learn by heart
verse is another word for poetry

explanation.surface: A literature seminar: talk it over and read some poems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Study' looks like part of the instruction, but it gives the old verb CON, to pore over.
explanation.definitionFit: To converse is to talk together, which is what people do when they discuss something.

clue.text: According to him it is reliable as a spaniel

definitions.text: According to him it is reliable

explanation.surface: A dog breed vouched for as dependable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'According to Cocker' is an old British idiom for 'correct', after Edward Cocker, a 17th-century arithmetic author.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocker's arithmetic book was the trusted authority on sums; a cocker is also a breed of spaniel.

clue.text: Good and acceptable

explanation.surface: Two near-synonyms of approval.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is understated praise meaning pretty good, or merely passable and satisfactory.

clue.text: Revised ox dues lead to mass emigration

indicators.note: revised means altered, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Higher taxes on cattle drive people off the land.
explanation.definitionFit: An exodus is the departure of many people at once, like the Israelites leaving Egypt.

clue.text: An abbreviation for a brief period

explanation.surface: Explaining what a shortened word stands for.
explanation.definitionFit: A short spelling is a contraction of a word; a short spell is a little while.

clue.text: Start out to ignite the fireworks

explanation.surface: Setting out for the evening's display and lighting the rockets.
explanation.definitionFit: Setting off is beginning a journey; setting off a rocket is lighting or detonating it.

clue.text: Short letter upset court case deciding school uniform

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a note is a brief letter
a suit is a legal action in court

explanation.surface: A brief letter overturned a lawsuit about what pupils must wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns NOTE into ETON. 'Short' belongs to the definition of NOTE, not a trimming signal. Eton is a famous English public school.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eton suit, short jacket and wide collar, was the traditional dress of junior boys at Eton College.

clue.text: Butler's task was to provide a free trade policy

explanation.surface: A servant's duty compared to economic doctrine.
explanation.definitionFit: A butler opens the front door to callers; an open-door policy allows trade on equal terms to all nations.

clue.text: Pavement leading to the podiatry lab

explanation.surface: Directions along the walkway to the foot clinic.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is FOOT (podiatry treats feet) and PATH, short for pathology lab. In Britain the pavement is the footpath beside a road.
explanation.definitionFit: A footpath is a walkway for pedestrians, like a sidewalk; whimsically, a pathology lab for feet.

clue.text: Get the message that summery material is being worn

parts.note: cotton is a light fabric favoured in summer
clothes that are on are being worn

explanation.surface: Realising the light summer fabric is what someone is wearing.
explanation.definitionFit: To cotton on is informal for grasping or understanding something.

clue.text: Blackhead gets a pressing invitation!

explanation.surface: A blackhead seems to be begging to be squeezed.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits as COME, DO!, an urgent invitation; 'pressing' also puns on squeezing a spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedo is the medical term for a blackhead; 'come, do' is an insistent urging to join in.

clue.text: Price a lute broken by Senora Peron

indicators.note: by means next to, so one piece stands beside the other

parts.note: Eva Perón, the Argentine first lady, gives the name Eva

indicators.note: a broken instrument has its parts scattered, so the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Putting a value on a damaged lute that belonged to Eva Perón.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges A LUTE; Eva Perón was the wife of Argentina's President Juan Perón, so 'Senora Peron' points to her first name.
explanation.definitionFit: To price something is to set a value on it, which is what evaluating means.

clue.text: Exhausted when employed at high level

parts.note: employed in the sense of put to use
up means raised or aloft

explanation.surface: Worn out after being put to work high up.
explanation.definitionFit: Used up means consumed or spent, so with nothing left: exhausted.

clue.text: Goldilocks?

parts.note: read the fairy-tale name literally as golden locks of hair

explanation.surface: The girl from the tale of the three bears.
explanation.definitionFit: Locks are tresses, and gold ones are a fair or yellow head of tresses.

clue.text: Put simply, it means to read the letters one by one

definitions.text: to read the letters one by one

explanation.surface: An explanation of what it means to make something plain.
explanation.definitionFit: To spell it out is to explain very plainly, and literally to name each letter of a word in turn.

clue.text: To request sex appeal is to invite trouble

parts.note: to ask for something is to request it
it was 1920s slang for sex appeal, as in the It girl

explanation.surface: Seeking allure only brings problems.
explanation.definitionFit: To be asking for it is to behave in a way that provokes trouble.

clue.text: A pyknic type begins a bout of fisticuffs

explanation.surface: A stocky man starts a fist fight.
explanation.walkthrough: Pyknic describes a short, stout, rounded body build.
explanation.definitionFit: A plump stocky person is literally a rounded individual; the opening round starts a boxing match.

clue.text: Attic reveals three different articles containing nickel

indicators.note: the three words hold the next piece between them

parts.note: the indefinite article a
the definite article the
the indefinite article an
Ni is the chemical symbol for nickel

explanation.surface: A loft turns up three newspaper pieces with some metal inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attic' looks like a loft but is the adjective for Attica, the region round Athens.
explanation.definitionFit: Attic means belonging to Attica or its capital, Athens, so an Attic citizen is from Athens.

clue.text: Exaggerate what the harpooners do

explanation.surface: Whalers telling tall tales about their catch.
explanation.definitionFit: Shooting a line is slang for bragging or exaggerating; harpooners literally fire a rope-trailing harpoon.

clue.text: Not clear barley soup

indicators.note: barley soup is a mush, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A cloudy bowl of barley broth.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleary eyes or images are dim and blurred, not sharp.

clue.text: Noted work by boy joining reserve force

parts.note: a son is a male child, a boy
by can mean per, as in rates by the day, and per is written as a in phrases like twice a day
the TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A piece of music composed by a lad who has signed up for the reserves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noted' means set in musical notes, not famous. A for 'by' is a stretch: it rests on 'by' meaning per, written as A.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonata is a musical composition, typically for one or two instruments, written in notes.

clue.text: Not cordial that is meant for a native worker

parts.note: a cool reception is unfriendly, not warm
i.e. is the abbreviation of Latin id est, that is

explanation.surface: An unfriendly drink set aside for a labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a dated colonial term for an Asian labourer, now considered offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: The word was used for a hired unskilled labourer in India or China.

clue.text: He foils a paling workman

explanation.surface: A man who thwarts plans and also puts up garden fences.
explanation.definitionFit: A fencer fights with a foil, a fencing sword; one who builds fences of palings is also a fencer.

clue.text: Rich oil-sheik's property leads to altercation

parts.note: an oil sheik owns an oil well
a to-do is a fuss or quarrel

explanation.surface: A wealthy sheik's oilfield sparks a dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-to-do means prosperous, comfortably wealthy.

clue.text: Castle that is suitable for raw recruit

parts.note: the castle in chess is also called a rook
i.e. is the abbreviation of Latin id est, that is

explanation.surface: A fortress deemed fit for a new soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Castle' looks like a building, but it is the chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A rookie is a newcomer or novice, especially a new recruit.

clue.text: What visitors do to meet the telephone charge

explanation.surface: Guests making a social visit, or settling the phone bill.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay a call is to visit someone; literally it is paying for a telephone call.

clue.text: Sentimental New York maid

parts.note: twee means affectedly quaint or sentimental

explanation.surface: A soppy housemaid from Manhattan.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweeny was a young between-maid who helped both cook and housemaid in a Victorian household.

clue.text: Dissolute merry age means she ain't what she used to be!

definitions.text: she ain't what she used to be!

indicators.note: dissolute means loose in morals, suggesting these letters are let loose and reordered

explanation.surface: Wild living in old age has taken its toll on her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dissolute' rearranges MERRY AGE. The definition quotes the American folk song 'The Old Grey Mare, she ain't what she used to be'.
explanation.definitionFit: The song's ageing horse is the subject of that refrain, so the quotation identifies her.
